source_refs.note: Topic 15.4 with the For Information box on the neuromuscular junction (PDF 33).

blocks.text: A synapse is the junction between the axon terminal of one neuron and the dendrites of another neuron or an effector cell of a muscle or gland. The two cells do not touch: a fluid-filled gap, the synaptic cleft, separates them. The neuron sending action potentials towards the synapse is the presynaptic neuron; the cell on the other side is the postsynaptic cell.

blocks.title: Neuromuscular junction
blocks.text: The synapse between a motor neuron and a muscle fibre is also called a neuromuscular junction.
